label: Strife opinion
summary: Changes the strife opinion caused by the character by the given amount.
details: The documented example runs it on a diarch with `15`. The game's documentation does not explain what strife opinion is beyond that. Vanilla mostly passes named script values such as minor_strife_gain, medium_strife_gain, major_strife_gain and major_strife_loss, so both gains and losses are used.

label: Phase
summary: Switches the struggle to a different phase that you name.
details: It changes straight to the named phase without passing through a transition phase, unless you ask for one with `with_transition = yes`. It works on a struggle. Vanilla writes it mostly as a block with `struggle_phase`.

fields.name: with_transition
fields.text: Whether the struggle goes through a transition phase on the way.

label: Phase duration
summary: Makes the struggle's current phase last longer or shorter.
details: The change is given either in points or in days, weeks, months or years, and can be negative. It works on a struggle. The input shows no vanilla use, so the game's documentation is the only source.

fields.name: duration
fields.text: How much to change the phase length by. Inside it, write either `points` or one of `days`, `weeks`, `months`, `years`.
fields.values: a number or a script value, can be negative

label: Target weight
summary: Changes the target weight of the character.
details: The game's documentation gives only the example `change_target_weight = 20` and does not say what the unit is or what the target weight does beyond its name. The base game never uses it.

label: Tenet popularity
summary: Raises or lowers how popular one tenet is within the faith.
details: It works on a faith. The change can be a number or a script value; vanilla uses named values such as minor_tenet_popularity_gain and major_tenet_popularity_loss. Vanilla's tenet is usually a saved scope or a `tenet:` key.

fields.name: target
fields.values: a tenet, or a saved scope holding one

fields.name: change
fields.values: a number or a script value, negative to lower it

label: Holder
summary: Hands the title to a new holder, using a title change you created earlier.
details: The title change (made beforehand with the game's title change effect) records the transfer, and this effect applies it. Vassals do not move with the title. If the title is a county, `take_baronies = yes` takes its baronies too, while without it they become vassals of the new holder. Vanilla uses it 656 times, nearly always with a saved scope as the change.

fields.name: holder
fields.text: The character who gets the title.

fields.name: change
fields.text: The previously created title change this transfer is added to.
fields.values: a saved scope holding a title change

fields.name: take_baronies
fields.text: For a county, whether its baronies are taken as well rather than made vassals.

fields.name: government_base
fields.text: A landed character whose government the new holder copies. The game's documentation says it is required when the holder has no land and the change is not of a kind such as appointment, election, stepped down or revoked.

label: Holder with vassals
summary: Hands the title to a new holder and moves its vassals to them as well.
details: It works like the plain holder change, but the vassals of the title go with it. A title change created earlier carries the details. For a county, `take_baronies = yes` takes its baronies too instead of making them vassals. Vanilla uses it far less often (76 times).

fields.name: holder
fields.text: The character who gets the title.

fields.name: change
fields.text: The previously created title change this transfer is added to.
fields.values: a saved scope holding a title change

fields.name: take_baronies
fields.text: For a county, whether its baronies are taken as well rather than made vassals.

fields.name: government_base
fields.text: A landed character whose government the new holder copies. Needed when the holder has no land and the change is not of a kind such as appointment, election, stepped down or revoked.

label: Title law level
summary: Moves a title's law in one law group a number of steps up or down the list.
details: It does not charge the usual law change costs and does not trigger the law's effects. Going past either end of the list stops at the last law there. Laws that would be invalid are not skipped.

fields.name: law_group
fields.text: The group of laws to move within.

fields.name: change
fields.values: a whole number, can be negative

label: Title law level (with effects)
summary: Moves a title's law in one law group a number of steps up or down, paying the law change costs and applying its effects.
details: It is the same as the plain title law level change, except that costs and effects of the law change do happen. Going past either end of the list stops at the last law there, and invalid laws are not skipped. The documented example uses the other key's name, which looks like a copy error; this key takes the same block.

fields.name: law_group
fields.text: The group of laws to move within.

fields.name: change
fields.values: a whole number, can be negative

label: Top phase
summary: Switches the top sub-region of the situation to a named phase.
details: It works on a situation. You can write the phase alone or in a block with `phase`. Vanilla uses it in block form, for example with reform_phase and concord.

label: Trait rank
summary: Moves a character up or down the ranks of a trait track.
details: Some traits come in ranks (for example the wounded track). `rank` is the change, so 1 moves up one rank and -1 down one. `max` caps the new rank. Vanilla mostly uses it on wounded and the education traits.

fields.name: trait
fields.text: The trait track (trait group) to change.

fields.name: rank
fields.values: a whole number, negative to go down

fields.name: max
fields.text: The highest rank the character may end up with.

label: Variable (change)
summary: Changes the value of a number variable by doing one calculation on it.
details: Pick one operation: add, subtract, multiply, divide, modulo, min or max. The value used can be a number, a script value or a saved scope that holds a value. Vanilla uses add by far the most, often with 1 or -1.

fields.name: modulo
fields.text: Replaces the variable with the remainder after division by this.

fields.name: min
fields.text: Sets the variable to the smaller of its value and this.

fields.name: max
fields.text: Sets the variable to the larger of its value and this.

label: War chest gold
summary: Adds gold to the great holy war's war chest, or takes it out with a negative amount.
details: It works on a great holy war. The amount is a script value, and vanilla also writes it as a block with `value` plus `multiply`, `divide` or `max` to shape the amount.

label: War chest piety
summary: Adds piety to the great holy war's war chest, or takes it out with a negative amount.
details: It works on a great holy war. The amount is a script value; vanilla uses plain numbers such as 75 up to 1200 and their negatives.

label: War chest prestige
summary: Adds prestige to the great holy war's war chest, or takes it out with a negative amount.
details: It works on a great holy war. The amount is a script value; vanilla uses plain numbers such as 250 up to 3000 and their negatives.

label: Worldliness
summary: Raises or lowers the worldliness of a holy order.
details: It works on a holy order. The game's documentation does not say what worldliness does, how big the numbers are, or what form the value takes, and vanilla has no use of it.

label: Clamp global variable
summary: Keeps a global variable between a lowest and a highest value.
details: A value above the maximum is set to the maximum, and one below the minimum is set to the minimum. The documented example is written with the plain clamp_variable name, so the exact form for this key is taken from there.

label: Clamp local variable
summary: Keeps a local variable between a lowest and a highest value.
details: A value above the maximum is set to the maximum, and one below the minimum is set to the minimum. The documented example is written with the plain clamp_variable name, so the exact form for this key is taken from there.

label: Clamp variable
summary: Keeps a variable between a lowest and a highest value.
details: A value above the maximum is set to the maximum, and one below the minimum is set to the minimum.

label: Clear appointment timeout
summary: Removes the waiting period that stops a character from taking part in appointments.
details: It clears any such timeout for any appointment. It works on a character and takes `yes`.

label: Clear artifact modifiers
summary: Removes all modifiers from an artifact.
details: It works on an artifact and takes `yes`.

label: Clear claimant
summary: Removes the claimant from a war.
details: It works on a war and takes `yes`. The game's documentation does not say what happens to the war's goal.

label: Clear culture traditions
summary: Removes all traditions from a culture.
details: It works on a culture and takes `yes`. The game's documentation does not say what else changes.

label: Clear designated heir
summary: Removes the heir the character has chosen, if there is one.
details: After this the character has no designated heir. It works on a character and takes `yes`.

label: Clear fallback succession
summary: Removes the fallback successor (a character or a title) the character has set.
details: It works on a character and takes `yes`.

label: Clear father
summary: Removes the character's father without putting anyone in his place.
details: It is meant for mods. A secret real father who has not been revealed is not removed; use the real father key for that.

label: Clear forced vote
summary: Removes a forced vote from the character.
details: The game's documentation says only that it clears forced voting and gives no more detail. It works on a character and takes `yes`.

label: Clear global variable list
summary: Empties a global variable list.
details: Give it the list's name, for example hre_elector_list, as vanilla does.

label: Clear house relation
summary: Removes the relation between two houses.
details: It runs on the house relation itself, written as `clear_house_relation = yes`.

label: Clear leading house
summary: Removes the leading house of a confederation.
details: With `no` the leading house is kept, so the key only does something with `yes`.

label: Clear legend chapter
summary: Empties the text of one named chapter of a legend.
details: It clears the localization key (the text reference) stored for that chapter. The documented example uses the chapter name `opening`.

label: Clear local variable list
summary: Empties a local variable list.
details: Give it the list's name.

label: Clear mother
summary: Removes the character's mother without putting anyone in her place.
details: It is meant for mods. A secret real mother who has not been revealed is not removed; use the real mother key for that.

label: Clear puppet status
summary: Frees a puppet from the one who controls them.
details: Nothing happens if the character is not a puppet. It works on the puppet and takes `yes`.

label: Clear real father
summary: Removes the character's real father, the one that can stay unrevealed and differ from the known father.
details: It is meant for mods and puts no one in his place. It works on a character.

label: Clear real mother
summary: Removes the character's real mother, the one that can stay unrevealed and differ from the known mother.
details: It is meant for mods and puts no one in her place. It works on a character.

label: Clear saved scope
summary: Forgets a saved scope, so `scope:<name>` no longer points to anything.
details: It clears the name from the top scope, the one the script block started in. Give it the name without `scope:`. It is the reverse of `save_scope_as`. Vanilla uses it often (189 times).

label: Clear supply
summary: Empties the supply of an army.
details: It works on an army and takes `yes`. The game's documentation does not say what the army suffers as a result.

label: Clear title laws
summary: Removes all laws from a title.
details: It does not charge the law removal costs and does not apply their effects. Use the effects version if you want those. It works on a title and takes `yes`.

label: Clear title laws (with effects)
summary: Removes all laws from a title, paying the law removal costs and applying their effects.
details: It is the same as the plain clear title laws, except that costs and effects do happen. It works on a title and takes `yes`.
